source_text: O altitudo divitiarum sapientiae et scientiae Dei! qui extra futuram operum retributionem ex multa parte liberum arbitrium formam voluit implere iudicii. Iustissime eum sibi bonus homo malusque committitur, ut et bonus se fruatur, et malus se ipse patiatur Non coniugalem, hoc est licitum honestumque concubitum, fuisse prohibitum, sed ut operis huius causa sit voluntas propaginis, non carnis voluptas; et quod sine libidine fieri non potest, sic tamen fiat, ut non propter libidinem fiat
pass_a_gloss: O altitudo divitiarum sapientiae and scientiae of-God! who outside futuram operum retributionem from many-things parte free decision formam voluit implere iudicii. Iustissime him to-himself good human-being evil-and committitur, so-that/as and good himself fruatur, and evil himself himself patiatur not coniugalem, this is licitum honestumque concubitum, to-have-been prohibitum, but so-that/as of-the-work of-this case/cause may-be will propaginis, not of-flesh pleasure; and that/which without by-lust to-become not is-able, thus nevertheless fiat, so-that/as not because-of lust fiat.

lemmas.lexica: LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium

pass_b_english: O the depth of the riches of God’s wisdom and knowledge (Romans 11:33)! Besides the future repayment of deeds, he willed free choice in large part to fulfill the form of judgment. Most justly, the good person and the evil person are each entrusted to themselves, so that the good person may enjoy himself and the evil person suffer himself.

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Linked from Julian's wording or a clear allusion in the excerpt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
